title: Mechanism of N-butanol extract of Pulsatilla decoction protected vaginal epithelial cells against Candida albicans infection by HIF-1alpha signaling and glucose metabolism revealed by transcriptomics and molecular docking.
authors: Chu, Faqiong; Wu, Hui; Li, Can; Zhao, Yiting; Wu, Daqiang; Feng, Xin; Wang, Tianming; Wang, Changzhong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究白头翁汤正丁醇提取物通过HIF-1alpha信号和糖代谢保护阴道上皮细胞免受白色念珠菌感染，分子对接仅用于药物-蛋白结合验证，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法聚焦TF-DNA结合建模。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Infection of vaginal epithelial cells by Candida albicans (C. albicans) can cause vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC). Pulsatilla decoction has been reported and used to treat VVC, but the specific mechanism of its protective effect on cells is still unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: In this study, transcriptomic profiling and molecular docking were used to predict the protective effects and regulatory mechanisms of the n-butanol extract of Pulsatilla Decoction (BEPD) in vaginal epithelial cells stimulated with C. albicans hyphae, and these findings were further validated experimentally. MATERIALS AND METHODS: To prepare the n-butanol extract from Pulsatilla decoction, transcriptome analysis was performed to identify significantly enriched genes and signaling pathways in vaginal epithelial cells stimulated with C. albicans hyphae. RT-qPCR was used to detect the expression levels of genes related to the HIF-1alpha pathway. Molecular docking was employed to verify the interactions between the main active components of BEPD and HIF-1alpha, as well as glucose metabolism-related proteins within the pathway. Immunofluorescence was used to detect the expression levels of HIF-1alpha, PFK2, ENO1, PDK1, Glut1, and LDHA. The cellular contents of ATP, lactic acid, and LDH were measured to reflect changes in sugar metabolism-related products. Western blot and ELISA were used to determine the levels of inflammatory factors such as IL-1beta and IL-2 in vaginal epithelial cells stimulated by C. albicans hyphae and treated with BEPD. RESULTS: BEPD exhibits a significant protective effect on vaginal epithelial cells stimulated by C. albicans hyphae. Transcriptomic analysis, including GO enrichment and KEGG pathway analysis, indicates that BEPD can regulate HIF-1alpha and its associated glucose metabolism disturbances in vaginal epithelial cells exposed to C. albicans hyphae. RT-qPCR confirmed the upregulation of HIF-1alpha gene expression in cells following BEPD treatment, while promoting the downregulation of genes related to anaerobic metabolism and attenuating the downregulation of genes involved in aerobic metabolism. Furthermore, studies on the binding interactions between drug compounds and cellular proteins revealed that the primary active components of BEPD can specifically bind to HIF-1alpha and proteins related to glucose metabolism. Immunofluorescence and Western blot analyses of HIF-1alpha and glucose metabolism-related proteins demonstrated that BEPD treatment results in significant upregulation of HIF-1alpha protein expression, which, in turn, markedly reduces the expression of genes associated with anaerobic metabolism and proteins involved in aerobic metabolism. ELISA assays further showed that BEPD can protect vaginal epithelial cells stimulated by C. albicans hyphae and decrease the expression levels of inflammatory factors in these cells. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that BEPD exerts a protective effect on vaginal epithelial cells stimulated by C. albicans hyphae. The underlying mechanism may involve the regulation of HIF-1alpha signaling and glucose metabolism homeostasis, which represents a novel mechanism against C. albicans infection. These findings provide a new theoretical basis for the prevention and treatment of vulvovaginal candidiasis, and further studies in animal models and clinical settings are warranted in the future.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：白色念珠菌（C. albicans）感染阴道上皮细胞可导致外阴阴道念珠菌病（VVC）。白头翁汤已被报道并用于治疗VVC，但其对细胞保护作用的具体机制仍不清楚。研究目的：本研究采用转录组学分析和分子对接技术，预测白头翁汤正丁醇提取物（BEPD）对白色念珠菌菌丝刺激的阴道上皮细胞的保护作用及调控机制，并通过实验进一步验证这些发现。材料与方法：制备白头翁汤正丁醇提取物，进行转录组分析以识别白色念珠菌菌丝刺激的阴道上皮细胞中显著富集的基因和信号通路。采用RT-qPCR检测与HIF-1α通路相关基因的表达水平。利用分子对接验证BEPD主要活性成分与HIF-1α及通路内葡萄糖代谢相关蛋白之间的相互作用。采用免疫荧光检测HIF-1α、PFK2、ENO1、PDK1、Glut1和LDHA的表达水平。测定细胞中ATP、乳酸和LDH的含量，以反映糖代谢相关产物的变化。采用Western blot和ELISA检测白色念珠菌菌丝刺激并经BEPD处理的阴道上皮细胞中IL-1β和IL-2等炎症因子的水平。结果：BEPD对白色念珠菌菌丝刺激的阴道上皮细胞表现出显著的保护作用。转录组分析（包括GO富集和KEGG通路分析）表明，BEPD能够调节暴露于白色念珠菌菌丝的阴道上皮细胞中HIF-1α及其相关的葡萄糖代谢紊乱。RT-qPCR证实，BEPD处理后细胞中HIF-1α基因表达上调，同时促进厌氧代谢相关基因的下调，并减弱有氧代谢相关基因的下调。此外，药物化合物与细胞蛋白之间的结合相互作用研究显示，BEPD的主要活性成分能够特异性结合HIF-1α及葡萄糖代谢相关蛋白。对HIF-1α和葡萄糖代谢相关蛋白的免疫荧光和Western blot分析表明，BEPD处理导致HIF-1α蛋白表达显著上调，进而显著降低厌氧代谢相关基因和有氧代谢相关蛋白的表达。ELISA检测进一步表明，BEPD能够保护白色念珠菌菌丝刺激的阴道上皮细胞，并降低这些细胞中炎症因子的表达水平。结论：本研究证明BEPD对白色念珠菌菌丝刺激的阴道上皮细胞具有保护作用。其潜在机制可能涉及调节HIF-1α信号通路和葡萄糖代谢稳态，这代表了对抗白色念珠菌感染的一种新机制。这些发现为外阴阴道念珠菌病的预防和治疗提供了新的理论基础，未来有必要在动物模型和临床环境中进行进一步研究。
